Users without `can_organize` now get 403 on create, update and delete for tags, categories and foods, and on `PUT /api/foods/merge`. A refused call changes nothing. The four new tests pass. I also ran the household, category/tag/tool and recipe test folders and they pass. I did not run the full backend suite.

- **Checks added:** I added `self.checks.can_organize()` as the first line of each of those handlers, in `controller_tags.py`, `controller_categories.py` and `foods.py`.
- **Latent bug fixed:** The `checks` property in `mealie/routes/_base/base_controllers.py` read `self._checks`, which was only annotated and never given a value. Calling it would have raised `AttributeError`. I gave `_checks` a default of `None`.
- **Reads:** Reads have no check, so GET on the collections and on single items still answers 200 whatever the flag.
- **Request time:** The user is loaded from the database on every request, for both session tokens and API tokens. Granting or removing the flag therefore applies on the next request.

The new tests are in `tests/integration_tests/user_household_tests/test_can_organize.py`. They flip the flag on and off and cover the 201, 200 and 403 cases, reads while the flag is off, and merge.
